title and abstract.summary: The study measured changes in species diversity and six functional traits (trophic level, seasonal duration, body size, elevational range, nesting position, and soil dependency) for different feeding guilds within the Aculeata community along an elevational gradient in a boreal forest.

methods.summary: This study measured the collection of Aculeata bees and wasps using yellow pan traps across different elevation sites in the Ashoro Research Forest and Mt. Kumaneshiri-dake.

results.summary: This study measured various ecological metrics, such as species richness, diversity indices, and community composition, across different feeding guilds (pollinators, predators, parasitoids) within Aculeata communities as a function of increasing elevation. The measurements covered multiple species within the studied groups. This study measured various ecological traits and community characteristics, such as trophic level, seasonal duration, nesting position, and diversity, across different elevation gradients for both parasitoid communities and specific insect groups.
